source_title: Analysis of Attractive Elements of Female Characters in Mobile Games
abstracted_dimensions: questionnaire evidence distinguishes incentive attraction from attraction that continues after exposure
factor analysis is used to examine combinations of attractive elements rather than a single element
incentive-attraction elements make an early impression while continuous-attraction elements can be added later to settings
the authors explicitly leave cross-game replication as future work, bounding generalization
reuse_note: Used only to derive a compositional distinction between immediate and persistent character appeal. The study's female-character and mobile-game scope is not generalized to every audience, gender, medium, or culture; no item wording, character, game, prose, image, or design was copied.
mechanisms: one high-salience signature cue establishes quick recognition without defining the whole character
a core personality tendency supplies continuity across situations
a repeatable habit or task behavior converts the tendency into visible evidence
a social or occupational role constrains which expressions and actions are plausible
a relationship stance changes distance, gaze, and care behavior toward a specific counterpart
a situational state modifies the baseline without erasing it
one controlled contrast or delayed reveal adds depth after the baseline is legible
attribute weights vary by audience and exposure, so the graph stores alternatives instead of a universal score
compatibility_rules: combine at most one primary visual anchor with one primary behavior and one relationship or context cue
let supporting appearance cues reinforce an observable action instead of standing alone as personality labels
use a contrast only after the baseline trait remains readable in the same scene
keep role, prop, and behavior causally connected so each cue explains another cue
allow alternative attribute bundles for different audiences rather than ranking one body, gender expression, or face as universally preferable
conflict_rules: reject bundles with several equally dominant costumes, accessories, expressions, and occupations
reject a claimed personality when every visible cue is purely decorative
reject role props that have no plausible task or handling relationship with the subject
reject combinations that require mutually incompatible simultaneous emotional states without an explicit suppression or contrast mechanism
reject a style tag that silently changes age, body, gender presentation, culture, or species against the user concept
counterexamples: a cute face and fashionable outfit with no character-specific action
a list of hair, eye, accessory, and costume tags whose elements do not interact
a single surprised expression treated as a stable personality
two unrelated archetypes placed together without a shared role, relationship, or reveal logic
boundaries: moe is not treated as synonymous with sexualization, youth, femininity, submissiveness, or a specific body type
no minor-coded body or school cue is sexualized, and adult characters remain the default for romantic framing
no race, nationality, disability, neurotype, body shape, occupation, or gender expression is used as a shortcut for personality
no copyrighted character, franchise costume, signature emblem, proprietary prop, or recognizable design bundle is reconstructed
no generated still is presented as evidence for diagnosing a real person's personality
locale terms remain market-specific and are not forced into one universal translation

term_notes.ja: 萌え and 萌え要素 may refer to an affective response or to elements associated with that response; neither is flattened into かわいい alone.
term_notes.en: moe and moe element are transliterations used as scoped media-study terms, not universal synonyms for cute, attractive, or desirable.
term_notes.ko: 모에 and 모에 요소 are treated as borrowed subculture labels and kept distinct from the broader everyday category 귀여움; the cited study does not establish a Korean universal taxonomy.
term_notes.zh: 萌, 萌点, and 萌系 are retained as adjacent Chinese-market labels rather than asserted one-to-one equivalents of Japanese 萌え; this matrix does not claim a validated Chinese taxonomy.

source_title: Male and Female Game Players’ Preferences for Game Characters and Real-world Personalities in Japan
abstracted_dimensions: in-depth interviews with 20 young game players in Japan explore why particular game characters are preferred
participants describe discovering hidden or unusual character aspects as gap-moe
contradictory characteristics or behaviors can become likable when the contrast is perceived as part of the same character
participants notice both stereotypical and non-stereotypical aspects, while the authors bound generalization because of the small, specific sample
reuse_note: Used to abstract gap-moe as an audience-recognized relation between a legible baseline and a hidden or contradictory aspect. The qualitative sample comprised 20 young game players in Japan and is not generalized by gender, culture, or medium; no participant quote, game, character, plot, image, or design was copied.
mechanisms: an observable public role or habitual presentation establishes the audience's initial expectation
a second trait is withheld from the first read but remains compatible with the same character history
a specific person, object, task, or privacy condition triggers the reveal
the contrast occupies one named axis such as role versus habit or competence versus vulnerability
a continuity anchor such as a repeated prop, posture, value, or goal keeps both sides recognizably one character
the reveal changes how the baseline is interpreted rather than deleting the baseline
relationship-specific access explains why one counterpart sees a softer, awkward, playful, or meticulous side
contrast intensity is bounded so surprise remains readable rather than becoming arbitrary inconsistency
compatibility_rules: establish the baseline with at least two mutually reinforcing cues before adding one contrast cue
make the unexpected side emerge from an action, relationship, or handled object instead of a caption
preserve a shared value, goal, or object across both sides so the contrast deepens identity
use one primary contrast axis per image and let minor cues support it
make the reveal context plausible for the role, setting, and relationship
conflict_rules: reject a surprise trait that has no trigger, history, or continuity anchor
reject multiple unrelated opposites that reduce the character to random novelty
reject a contrast that replaces competence, agency, or established values solely to make the subject helpless
reject captions, interface text, or internal monologue as the only evidence of the gap
reject culturally gendered expectations as if they were natural laws
counterexamples: a costume associated with one role while the character simply smiles
a continuity or anatomy error mistaken for intentional contradiction
a serious character making an arbitrary comic face with no relationship or trigger
a hidden trauma, disability, identity, or private status used as a cute surprise
boundaries: no masculinity-femininity binary is required to create contrast
no transgender identity, cross-gender performance, sexual orientation, or private identity is framed as a deceptive reveal
no disability, neurodivergence, illness, poverty, trauma, or abuse is used as an endearing twist
no cruelty, coercion, stalking, humiliation, or controlling behavior is redeemed by one soft gesture
no copyrighted character, costume, scene, quote, signature object, or franchise-specific contrast is reproduced
the small Japanese interview sample supports a mechanism candidate, not a universal preference claim

term_notes.ja: ギャップ萌え is source-supported as affection arising when hidden, unusual, or contradictory aspects become visible; it is an audience response, not merely any inconsistency.
term_notes.en: gap moe is retained as a transliterated media-studies term and modeled as baseline plus reveal plus continuity, not as a generic plot twist.
term_notes.ko: 갭모에 is treated as a borrowed fandom label; 반전 매력 is an adjacent Korean phrase but is not asserted as an exact scholarly synonym by these sources.
term_notes.zh: 反差萌 is retained as an adjacent Chinese-market label, but this evidence set does not establish exact equivalence with Japanese ギャップ萌え or a universal contrast taxonomy.

source_title: Expressing Personality Through Non-verbal Behaviour in Real-Time Interaction
abstracted_dimensions: the virtual-human model controls gaze, facial expression, gesture, and posture as separate nonverbal behavior channels
the implemented personality space is explicitly limited to extraversion-introversion and stability-neuroticism dimensions
personality parameters affect internal affective state and the probability or manner of behavior execution
passive ratings and live interaction studies test whether observers attribute the intended personality configurations
reuse_note: Used to derive a fictional-character behavior grammar from empirically tested nonverbal channels. The study models virtual humans mainly along extraversion and stability dimensions; it does not justify diagnosing real people or inferring traits from bodies or faces, and no stimulus, parameter table, software behavior, prose, avatar, or image was copied.
mechanisms: a trait is represented as a recurring distribution of actions rather than one symbolic pose
a situational trigger selects which plausible behavior becomes visible
gaze establishment, maintenance, and release show attention toward a person or task
gesture frequency and spatial extent modulate social energy without changing anatomy
posture lean and posture shifts express approach, reserve, confidence, or uncertainty in context
self-adaptor behavior can signal transient regulation but never defines a trait alone
facial action magnitude and gaze are coordinated with hand and body channels
high-priority task reactions suppress irrelevant idle behavior
current affect changes the intensity of behavior while the longer-term character baseline remains recognizable
compatibility_rules: pair every abstract trait label with an observable action, target, and situation
use two or three coordinated channels rather than forcing every face, hand, gaze, and posture cue at once
let task and relationship cues explain why the selected behavior appears now
treat the still image as one plausible sample from a repeated pattern, not proof of the whole personality
separate baseline trait, current emotion, and intentional gap-moe contrast into different fields
conflict_rules: reject personality adjectives with no visible behavioral evidence
reject skull, eye shape, body type, skin, disability, clothing culture, or gender presentation as personality proof
reject incompatible gaze, hand, task, and body targets unless a deliberate conflict mechanism is specified
reject idle gestures that occlude or contradict the primary task action
reject intensity stacks that turn subtle characterization into theatrical noise
counterexamples: folded arms alone treated as proof of hostility
an averted gaze alone treated as proof of shyness or dishonesty
a tidy room alone treated as proof of conscientiousness
one smile treated as a permanent cheerful personality
a mobility aid, tremor, tic, scar, or sensory behavior treated as a personality cue
boundaries: the grammar stages fictional behavior and must never be used to diagnose or rank a real person
single-frame evidence is explicitly weaker than repeated behavior across situations
no physiognomy, racialized coding, gender essentialism, body-size moralizing, or class-based character judgment
no disability, neurodivergence, illness, trauma response, or culturally specific gesture is assigned a universal personality meaning
behavior channels must respect anatomy, accessibility equipment, and the subject's requested cultural context
the source's virtual-human findings are used as compositional guidance, not as a complete theory of personality

term_notes.ja: 性格 is kept distinct from a momentary 感情 or 状態; しぐさ and 言動 are observable evidence channels, not deterministic labels.
term_notes.en: personality trait means a tendency across time and situations, while state or emotion describes the current moment; the image encodes one fictional behavioral sample.
term_notes.ko: 성격 and 캐릭터성 are not collapsed into 현재 감정 or 분위기; 행동 증거 describes staging evidence, not a real-person assessment.
term_notes.zh: 性格 is kept distinct from 情绪 and 状态, while 人设 can include broader authored persona or setting; none is treated as an exact substitute for repeated behavior.

source_title: ツンデレキャラクターのリアクション統計分析を適用したツンデレ対話モデルの構築
abstracted_dimensions: tsundere is defined in the cited paper as outwardly cold or harsh speech and actions with occasional glimpses of affection
the study encodes reactions to multiple situations together with underlying true-feeling state across seven parameter groups
factor analysis is used to extract characteristic reaction patterns, including outward attitude that differs from underlying feeling
the paper applies the extracted properties to a dialogue model using two-dimensional morphing and probabilistic methods
reuse_note: Used to replace fixed dere archetype presets with context, relationship, outward reaction, underlying feeling, and intensity axes. The paper analyzes a small set of well-known tsundere characters and does not validate the entire '-dere' vocabulary across media or cultures; no character, dialogue, reaction data, factor loading, model asset, prose, image, or design was copied.
mechanisms: relationship target determines whether warmth, reserve, rivalry, respect, or protectiveness is relevant
a situation trigger such as help, praise, embarrassment, risk, error, or privacy selects the response
outward reaction valence is stored separately from underlying affiliative intent
public-private visibility changes how much warmth the character permits to show
affection latency controls whether care appears immediately, after hesitation, or only through a practical act
verbal distance and physical distance remain independent axes
protective or supportive action can carry warmth even when the face remains restrained
suppression leakage allows one small involuntary cue to coexist with deliberate composure
repair and recovery behavior after a harsh response determine whether the pattern reads as care or merely hostility
compatibility_rules: specify relationship, trigger, outward reaction, underlying intent, and visible action together
use one dominant behavioral axis and at most one secondary leakage cue in a still image
prefer practical care and repair behavior over blush as the primary evidence of warmth
keep harshness proportional and non-abusive so the caring mechanism remains credible
let public or private context explain why the same character expresses different warmth levels
conflict_rules: reject a dere label with no relationship target or situation trigger
reject hair style, eye color, costume, body type, or gender as proof of a dere pattern
reject severe humiliation, assault, coercion, stalking, or control followed by one affectionate cue as reconciliation
reject every channel simultaneously showing opposite extremes without a suppression hierarchy
reject labels from different locales as interchangeable presets when their usage has not been validated
counterexamples: a quiet character automatically classified as dandere
an expressionless or competent character automatically classified as kuudere
blushing alone treated as affection or consent
possessiveness, surveillance, threats, or isolation framed as intense care
generic rudeness with no repair, vulnerability, or prosocial action called tsundere
boundaries: no abuse, coercion, stalking, non-consensual control, or sexual harassment is romanticized as a dere trait
no mental illness, attachment diagnosis, trauma response, or personality disorder is mapped to a fandom label
no minor is sexualized and adult characters remain the default for romantic framing
no dere style is assigned by gender, body, race, class, disability, occupation, or national culture
no franchise character, signature dialogue pattern, costume, scene, or proprietary relationship arc is reproduced
the evidence directly supports tsundere mechanisms; other '-dere' labels remain unvalidated candidates and must be expressed through descriptive axes

term_notes.ja: ツンデレ is source-supported as a context-sensitive behavior pattern in which outward coldness or harshness can coexist with glimpses of affection; デレ is used only as a graded warmth or affection dimension here. クーデレ and ダンデレ are not defined by this evidence set.
term_notes.en: tsundere remains a transliteration, while the implementation uses descriptive axes such as affection latency and public-private warmth rather than treating '-dere' as a clinical personality class.
term_notes.ko: 츤데레 and 데레 are treated as borrowed subculture labels and kept distinct from generic 무뚝뚝함, 수줍음, or 다정함; this evidence does not validate a complete Korean dere taxonomy.
term_notes.zh: 傲娇 is retained as an adjacent Chinese localization for tsundere but is not asserted as an exact one-to-one equivalent in every market; descriptive reaction axes take precedence over the label.
